trust_decision.summary: A bundle is accepted only if at least `threshold` independently verified witnesses exist; the deciding counts are the Rekor-entry counter at pkg/verify/tlog.go:196-201 and the SCT counter at pkg/verify/sct.go:90-97, and at the pinned commit both count items (entries, SCT-chain pairs) rather than distinct logs, so one compromised log meets a multi-log threshold.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'multi-log threshold bypass via single compromised log', so an engineer opens the tlog threshold comparison first; the pre-existing duplicate-entry guard at pkg/verify/tlog.go:51-58, whose comment claims to stop duplicates being used 'to bypass the threshold', makes the function look already defended.

fix_sites.entry_point: verify.VerifyTlogEntry (public func); also reached by (*verify.Verifier).Verify via VerifyTransparencyLogInclusion (pkg/verify/signed_entity.go:812) and by the deprecated verify.VerifyArtifactTransparencyLog (pkg/verify/tlog.go:218)
verify.VerifyTlogEntry, whose returned []root.Timestamp is consumed by (*verify.Verifier).VerifyObserverTimestamps (pkg/verify/signed_entity.go:849-852)
verify.VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp (public func); reached by (*verify.Verifier).Verify when WithSignedCertificateTimestamps is set (pkg/verify/signed_entity.go:679)
verify.VerifySignedCertificateTimestamp (per-chain increment in the inner chains loop)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names the transparency log; the SCT check is a separate certificate-transparency check against a different trust root (TrustedMaterial.CTLogs() rather than RekorLogs()), enabled by a different verifier option (WithSignedCertificateTimestamps), its own error text counts 'SCT entries' not logs, and VerifyTlogEntry's doc (pkg/verify/tlog.go:38-39) only promises 'unique transparency log entries' - so sct.go reads as a neighbouring feature rather than the same protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Bundles legitimately carry more than one entry from the same log, and one certificate legitimately carries several SCTs; these must still verify at threshold 1 and still contribute exactly one integrated timestamp, so the fix must dedupe the count rather than reject duplicate-log items, and it must key the dedupe on the log's key ID, not on its BaseURL/URI - Rekor v1 trusted roots may leave BaseURL empty (pkg/verify/tlog.go:112 rejects v2 entries without it), and root.Timestamp.URI is set from BaseURL at pkg/verify/tlog.go:100, so copying isDuplicateTSA's URI dedupe (pkg/verify/tsa.go:67-74) would collapse distinct v1 logs. The repo's own pinned test pkg/verify/sct_test.go:357-386 asserts that two SCTs from one log meet a threshold of 2, i.e. it encodes the vulnerable behaviour as expected.

O6_input_shapes: several tlog entries with the same log key ID but different log index (the existing guard at pkg/verify/tlog.go:51-58 only rejects same key ID AND same index)
entries from one log where only some carry an inclusion promise (HasInclusionPromise) and others only an inclusion proof
several SCTs embedded in one leaf certificate that name the same CT log ID
one SCT that verifies against more than one chain returned by cert.Verify (pkg/root/certificate_authority.go:65), inflating the per-chain counter

O7_producer.where: pkg/bundle/bundle.go:300-327 materialises []*tlog.Entry from the bundle's protobuf/JSON tlog entries; the identity the count keys on is produced by pkg/tlog/entry.go:402-404 (LogKeyID() returns the raw LogId.KeyId bytes as a string)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a TSA threshold that counts verified timestamps without deduping per authority
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same count-until-threshold helper is written three times (tlog.go, sct.go, tsa.go); the URI-keyed isDuplicateTSA at pkg/verify/tsa.go:67-74 is that mechanism written a third time, so a new option could easily omit it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an integrated-timestamp threshold that counts len(logTimestamps) with no dedupe of its own
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it consumes the tlog producer's slice, so a maintainer adding a further timestamp option would naturally re-count the slice instead of the distinct logs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-bundle-version branch that materialises tlog entries and enforces its own per-log rule
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the version switch at pkg/bundle/bundle.go:101-124 already special-cases inclusion promise vs proof per bundle version, so a per-version log-count rule is a plausible addition on the deserialization path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second log-identity accessor (for example keyed on the log's base URL) that a count could key on
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Entry exposes both LogKeyID() and the raw TransparencyLogEntry(), so a counter keyed on GetLogId().KeyId versus the verifier's own ID is an easy divergence to write.

O9_family: CWE-345/CWE-347 improper verification of a cryptographic signature: a threshold is satisfied by non-distinct witnesses (verification bypass via one compromised transparency log)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0 (go.mod:3); modules resolved from go.sum, no vendor directory present
O10_build.project_tests: pkg/verify/tlog_test.go, sct_test.go, tsa_test.go and signed_entity_test.go cover this area and run offline against the in-memory sigstore in pkg/testing/ca; test/e2e/e2e_test.go and test/conformance/main.go need a live Sigstore deployment. The pinned pkg/verify/sct_test.go:357-386 asserts the vulnerable expectation (two SCTs from one log meet a threshold of 2) and must be changed by a correct fix.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a dedupe keyed on the log's BaseURL/URI (mirroring isDuplicateTSA at pkg/verify/tsa.go:67-74) or reject any bundle carrying two entries from the same log, instead of counting distinct log key IDs.
